author: Herbert Spencer
title: The Man Versus the State
notes: Individualism vs. state intervention; echoes Mill, prefigures 20th-c classical liberalism and libertarianism.

author: James George Frazer
title: The Golden Bough (abridged)
notes: Myth, magic, ritual, religion across cultures. Enormous influence on 20th-c anthropology, literature (Eliot, Joyce), and theory.

author: G.W.F. Hegel
title: Lectures on the Philosophy of History
notes: Sibree translation. World spirit, historical development, dialectic in history. Bridges Phenomenology to Marx.

author: Ludwig Feuerbach
title: The Essence of Christianity
notes: Projection theory of religion; God as alienated human essence. Direct influence on Marx's alienation concept.

author: Oscar Wilde
title: Intentions
notes: The Decay of Lying, The Critic as Artist. Art for art's sake; aestheticism; anti-naturalism in criticism.

author: Leo Tolstoy
title: What is Art?
notes: Art as communication of feeling; critique of aestheticism and formalism. Influential counter-position to Wilde.

author: Henri Poincaré
title: Science and Hypothesis
notes: Conventionalism in science; role of hypothesis, geometry, and intuition. Key pre-Vienna Circle philosophy of science.

author: Benedetto Croce
title: Aesthetic as Science of Expression and General Linguistic
notes: Expression, intuition, and art as language. Foundational idealist aesthetics; influenced Collingwood and Italian culture broadly.

author: Henri Poincaré
title: The Value of Science
notes: Mathematical intuition, objectivity, and the nature of scientific truth. Companion to Science and Hypothesis.

author: John Dewey
title: How We Think
notes: Reflective thinking, inquiry, problem-solving. Foundational for pragmatist epistemology and education theory.

author: Clive Bell
title: Art
notes: Significant form; formalist aesthetics. Key Bloomsbury Group text; influenced mid-century art criticism.

author: Albert Einstein
title: Relativity: The Special and General Theory
notes: Popular exposition of special and general relativity. Introduces space-time, simultaneity, reference frames into broad discourse.

author: Bertrand Russell
title: Introduction to Mathematical Philosophy
notes: Logical foundations of mathematics; classes, relations, cardinal numbers. Bridges Principia Mathematica to philosophy of language.

author: T.S. Eliot
title: The Sacred Wood
notes: Tradition and the Individual Talent; impersonal theory of poetry. Foundational for Anglo-American literary modernism.

author: Roger Fry
title: Vision and Design
notes: Formalist art criticism; pure aesthetic response; design and significant form. Bloomsbury aesthetics alongside Clive Bell.

author: Alfred North Whitehead
title: Science and the Modern World
notes: Critique of scientific materialism; organism, process, and nature. Bridges Whitehead's process philosophy to philosophy of science.

author: Pierre Duhem
title: The Aim and Structure of Physical Theory
notes: Holism (Duhem-Quine thesis), underdetermination, theory-ladenness of observation. Foundational for 20th-c philosophy of science.

author: Rudolf Carnap
title: The Unity of Science
notes: Logical syntax, physicalism, unified science language. Vienna Circle manifesto text.

author: Otto Neurath, Rudolf Carnap, Charles Morris (eds.)
title: International Encyclopedia of Unified Science
notes: Unified science program; includes Kuhn's Structure of Scientific Revolutions as monograph. Logical empiricism in full.

author: Susanne Langer
title: Philosophy in a New Key
notes: Symbol, meaning, music, and art. Bridges analytic philosophy to aesthetics and semiotics; influenced design theory.

author: Charles Taylor
title: Sources of the Self
notes: Identity, moral frameworks, modernity, authenticity. Major work bridging continental and analytic traditions in moral philosophy.

author: Anthony Giddens
title: The Consequences of Modernity
notes: Structuration theory, reflexive modernity, trust, risk. Key late-century sociology bridging structure and agency.

author: Ulrich Beck
title: Risk Society
notes: Risk, reflexive modernization, second modernity. Foundational for sociology of risk and late-modern society.

author: Zygmunt Bauman
title: Life in Fragments
notes: Liquid modernity vocabulary; postmodern ethics, fragmented identity, ambivalence.

author: Jürgen Habermas
title: Between Facts and Norms
notes: Discourse theory of law and democracy; deliberative politics. Companion to Theory of Communicative Action.

author: Quentin Meillassoux
title: After Finitude
notes: Speculative realism, correlationism, contingency, the absolute. Central text of 2000s-2010s continental philosophy revival.

author: Graham Harman
title: Weird Realism: Lovecraft and Philosophy
notes: Object-oriented ontology (OOO); withdrawal, allure, vicarious causation. Key speculative realism text.

author: Bernard Stiegler
title: Technics and Time 3: Cinematic Time and the Question of Malaise
notes: Tertiary retention, cinematic consciousness, attention, malaise. Completes the Technics and Time trilogy.

author: Jacques Rancière
title: The Emancipated Spectator
notes: Distribution of the sensible, spectatorship, emancipation, aesthetics and politics.

author: Friedrich Nietzsche
title: The Gay Science
notes: Titled "The Joyful Wisdom" in the Common translation. God is dead, perspectivism, eternal recurrence, amor fati.

author: Wilhelm Wundt
title: Principles of Physiological Psychology
notes: First systematic experimental psychology textbook. Apperception, sensation, psychophysics. Foundational for cognitive science genealogy.

author: Alfred Tarski
title: Introduction to Logic
notes: Formal semantics, truth, deduction. Bridges Frege-Carnap formal tradition into natural language discourse. Key for tracking "truth" and "reference" vocabulary.

author: Charles Morris
title: Signs, Language and Behavior
notes: Synthesises Peirce semiotics with behaviorism. Bridges 1930s Peirce Collected Papers entry to post-war linguistics. Sign, signification, pragmatics.

author: Susanne Langer
title: Feeling and Form
notes: Follow-up to Philosophy in a New Key. Symbol, expression, form in art. Key for aesthetic vocabulary arc.

author: Alexander Galloway
title: Protocol
notes: Network, protocol, control, decentralization. Key for 2000s vocabulary around distributed systems and power.

author: Mark Hansen
title: New Philosophy for New Media
notes: Embodiment and digital media. Bridges phenomenology (Bergson, Merleau-Ponty) and digital image theory.

author: Marshall McLuhan
title: The Gutenberg Galaxy: The Making of Typographic Man
notes: Precedes Understanding Media. Typographic man, acoustic vs visual space, mosaic vs linear thought. Medium is the message first fully developed here.

author: Auguste Comte
title: The Positive Philosophy of Auguste Comte
notes: Hackett abridgment of Cours de philosophie positive. Foundational positivism vocabulary: positive, empirical, sociology, hierarchy of sciences.
